summary: Sound, rules-compliant base. The measured result (dfee6f2939974bad, 1.127x [1.111,1.144], 16/16) matches every expected direction, and nothing has landed that could confound it. Land it as a verbatim whole-file replacement of master's submission.py, not as a patch onto the held parity base. Fix two latent fragilities (contiguity assumptions, the lazy inv_freq table) before 12 dependents inherit them.
justification: Mechanism: SGLang's sliding and small full shapes are launch-bound (floors 0.1-4.3 us vs 21-36 us measured), and the kernel collapses FusedQKNorm(+RoPE), the k and v FP8 casts, store_cache and the q cast into one launch. The profile of dfee6f2939974bad confirms it: _pre_attention_kernel takes 1.3-2.7 us per shape and the remaining time is FA3 main, FA3 combine, prepare_varlen_num_blocks and norm_gate. Per-shape paired ratios: sliding decode_1 1.246, decode_16 1.298, decode_32 1.249, verify_1 1.334, verify_16 1.304, verify_32 1.194; full decode_1 1.127, verify_1 1.213 (both faster, as expected); full decode_16 1.029, decode_32 1.015, verify_16 1.036, verify_32 1.015 (expected flat; they come out slightly faster, as expected from saving a few us on 200-390 us). The expected list matches the TASK weights: the sliding shapes (weight 46) carry the gain. Weakest link: the RoPE angle precision at large positions. ang = float(pos) * inv_freq goes through tl.cos/tl.sin. If Triton lowers these to the approximate MUFU path (cos.approx.f32), the error grows with |angle| (up to about 8e4 rad at 80K context for i=0), whereas the reference uses accurate torch cos/sin on the same fp32 product. All 16 tests passed and every timed 80K sliding call was checked, so it is within bounds today. The margin against the 8% k-entry bound and the output bound is not known, and a dependent that changes rounding elsewhere (an extra bf16 hop, a different FP8 cast) could take the slack. A second, minor point: k and q go fp32 -> FP8 directly, while SGLang goes fp32 -> bf16 -> FP8. This is finer, not coarser, so it is allowed, but the bits differ from SGLang.
confounders: None: landed-muse_attention_decode.json is empty, and master is the plain-PyTorch starter (BEST 0.0023x). This hypothesis is itself the first base, so no landed change can share its launch sequence, memory traffic or numerics.
interference: No companion is warranted. The result already exists, and resubmitting identical code returns the same job. Nothing has landed to revert or tune. Splitting the sub-changes (q fused vs k/v store fused) would only re-attribute a gain that all comes from one mechanism (removing launches), and it would not change any dependent's interpretation. Each dependent measures against this base, so its own A/B is internal to its own change. The real risk to dependents is procedural, not statistical. The kernel lives only in the dirty working tree, and the hypothesis text says 'take that code verbatim onto the parity base', but sglang-path-parity is held and was never landed. Churnsubs must commit the .bak file as a whole-file replacement of master's submission.py (blob identical to the dfee6f2939974bad submission), so that every dependent's parent commit is that exact code and their baseline-relative numbers are comparable to 1.127x.
rules_flags: No hard violation found. No host syncs. torch.empty for q is shape-only. FP8 E4M3 queries are allowed. The cache stays FP8 and the output is BF16 via rms_norm_gate. FA3 is given the full window (window-1, 0) and the full context. All work is inside kernel_fn.

_INV_FREQ is filled lazily on the first call per (theta, d, device). It derives from config, not data, so it is legal caching. But if a graph capture ever happens before an eager call with that theta, the allocation and arange land inside the capture. Build it at import for theta=500000, or warm it up explicitly, so the base and all 12 dependents are robust to the judge's capture order.

The kernel indexes k_cache, v_cache and the q buffer with implicit contiguous strides ((loc*HKV+kh)*D) and assumes a unit inner stride on qkv. That is correct for the judge's tensors today (page_size 64 tests passed), but nothing asserts it. Add asserts or pass strides before upstreaming, so a dependent that changes the q layout (fa3-hdim128-head-pairing, fa3-batched-q-verify) cannot silently write to the wrong rows.

Numerics differ from SGLang: there is no bf16 rounding before the FP8 cast for q and k. This is allowed (finer, not coarser), but write it down, so a dependent claiming 'SGLang parity' numerics does not misattribute check-margin changes.
open_questions: Does tl.cos/tl.sin on fp32 lower to libdevice cosf/sinf or to cos.approx/sin.approx on this Triton version? If approx, how much of the 8% k-entry margin is left at position ~80K, and should the kernel compute angles with explicit range reduction (or a precomputed fp32 table via libdevice) to protect dependents?

What are the actual check margins (k-entry rel-L2 and output error vs bound) in submission.dfee6f2939974bad.log? Recording them in FINDINGS lets dependents see whether they ate into the precision slack.

The hypothesis body is stale ('check job ... queued, no result yet', 'onto the parity base'). Update it to the measured result, and set base to master with whole-file replacement, before churnsubs dispatches dependents.
